topic: High levels of agreeableness are correlated with lower life satisfaction
angle: While agreeableness is linked to higher marital satisfaction and positive affect, lower agreeableness is linked to higher job burnout.
title: The Cost of Agreeableness

reveal.headline: High agreeableness correlates with higher marital satisfaction.
reveal.body: The data shows that being agreeable is linked to better relationships and positive affect, rather than lower life satisfaction. The evidence on its impact on overall well-being remains mixed.

explain.headline: Agreeableness creates different outcomes for different lives.
explain.body: Agreeableness is linked to improved orthodontic outcomes and favorable treatment attitudes. However, it is also linked to higher levels of job burnout.

matters.headline: Your kindness may have a cost.
matters.body: That may be why you feel content in your private life but exhausted by your career. Your social harmony might be linked to your professional fatigue.

question.headline: Is your kindness a source of your exhaustion?

verdict: The evidence does not support the idea that high agreeableness leads to lower life satisfaction; instead, it is linked to higher marital satisfaction and positive affect.
caveat: The sources provide mixed results on how agreeableness impacts different types of well-being, such as marital satisfaction versus job burnout.
caption:
High agreeableness does not lead to lower life satisfaction.

Research shows agreeableness is linked to higher marital satisfaction and positive affect, but it is also linked to higher job burnout. The evidence on its impact on overall well-being is mixed.
